summary: Mr. Mosseri explains the traditional all-night reading of Shavuot, which consists of Torah, Nevi'im, Ketuvim, and the Idra Rabba from the Zohar. He details the historical practice of the community rabbis and discusses the custom regarding the timing of the morning prayers at sunrise.
questions: What is the traditional reading for the night of Shavuot?
How long is spent reading Tanakh versus the Zohar on Shavuot night?
Did the rabbis of the community hold classes on Shavuot night?
When should the morning prayers begin after the all-night reading?
